# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 25 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 25 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_025_page_001.jpg

---

## Vision 5 — The Transition to the Shepherd

**1** The vision of the fifth order that appeared to me, brothers and sisters, is as follows. **2** I was fasting and sitting on a certain mountain, giving thanks to God for all he had done for me, when I saw the Shepherd sitting beside me. He said: "Why have you come here so early?" I answered, "Because, sir, I keep a station here." **3** He said to me, "I am the angel of repentance. I have been sent to dwell with you for the rest of your life." **4** I suspected he was testing me. I said to him, "Who are you? I know to whom I have been entrusted, and who it is that dwells with me." He replied, "Do you not recognize me?" "No," I said. He said, "I am the Shepherd to whom you have been entrusted." **5** While he was speaking, his form was changed, and I recognized him as the one to whom I had been entrusted. Immediately I was overcome with confusion; fear seized me and I was overwhelmed with grief that I had answered him in such a rude and foolish manner. **6** He replied: "Do not be confused, but be strengthened in my commandments which I am about to give you. For I have been sent," he said, "to show you again all that you saw before, and especially the things that are most important for your life. First of all, keep my commandments, and you will be pleasing to God. **7** Write the Commandments and the Parables." **8** When he had finished speaking with me he rose and departed, and I could not see which way he went. There was a noise and I turned around in fear, thinking it was the beast. But when I looked, I saw nothing except the man sitting beside me.

---

*LOGOS note: "Station" (statio) = a Roman Christian fasting day (Wednesday and/or Friday). The angel's commissioning ("dwell with you for the rest of your life") is the basis for all subsequent moral instruction in the Mandates and Similitudes.*
